text: The Albany Medical Center Prize in Medicine and Biomedical Research is the United States' second-highest-value prize in medicine and biomedical research, awarded by the Albany Medical Center. Among global medical prizes, it ranks fourth in monetary value, following the $3 million Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences, the $1.2 million Nobel Prize in Medicine, and the $1 million Shaw Prize in life science and medicine. Awarded annually, the $500,000 prize is given to any physician, scientist, or group whose work has resulted in significant advances in health care and scientific research with demonstrated translational benefits applied to improved patient care. The prize honors the legacy of its founder, the late Morris "Marty" Silverman, who established a tradition at the inaugural ceremony in Albany, NY, in March 2001, promising to light one candle each year to honor the recipient. This tradition is set to continue for one hundred years, the full duration of the Prize. Press releases for the award have been issued annually from 2001 through 2025, with specific releases documented for the years 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021, 2019, 2018, 2017, 2016, 2015, 2014, 2013, 2012, 2011, 2010, 2009, 2008, 2007, 2006, 2005, and 2004 through 2002, with some years lacking a release.
